items.title: A Shipping-Center Break-In Just Handed Scammers 81,000 Customer Lists
items.summary: A gadget-wallet maker called Trezor just revealed that a break-in at its shipping partner now touches 81,000 customers — names, home addresses, phone numbers, and order details, some from orders placed years ago. Lists like this are gold for scammers pretending to be real stores, so expect very convincing fake emails, calls, and letters. Don't trust a caller just because they know your name and what you bought — hang up and call the company back using the number on its real website.

items.title: Your laptop says it's full but your photos are already safe — OneDrive's "Free up space" clears the clutter without deleting anything
items.summary: If your laptop keeps saying "storage full," open your OneDrive folder, right-click the biggest folders (usually Pictures), and choose **"Free up space."** The photo stays safe in the cloud at onedrive.com — your laptop keeps a small shortcut instead of the full copy. OneDrive is built into Windows 10 and 11, no download needed.

items.title: Hate the giant Windows 11 Start menu? The latest free update lets you shrink it and move the taskbar — here's the setting
items.summary: Install the latest free update via **Settings > Windows Update > Check for updates**, then open **Settings > Personalization > Start** to shrink the menu and hide sections you never use, and **Settings > Personalization > Taskbar > Taskbar behaviors** to move it where you want it.

items.title: Hackers Are Taking Over Home Routers Right Now — Check Yours Today
items.summary: Security researchers just caught criminals breaking into a popular brand of internet router and taking complete control — no password needed. If crooks get into your router, they can watch everything you do online and steer you to fake websites that steal your logins. Your best defense takes two minutes: unplug your router, count to ten, plug it back in, then check its settings for a software update — or call your internet company and ask them to update it for you.

items.title: The FTC just refreshed its phishing scam guide — learn the six tricks crooks use in fake emails, and report them free at reportfraud.ftc.gov
items.summary: The Federal Trade Commission updated its free phishing guide on September 1, 2026. It walks through the six stories scammers tell — fake "suspicious activity" alerts, bogus invoices, phony refunds, and too-good coupons — and shows exactly what to do if you already clicked. Read it free at **consumer.ftc.gov** (search "phishing scams"), and forward any suspicious email to the FTC at **reportfraud.ftc.gov** — it takes under two minutes and helps shut the crooks down.

items.title: Bitwarden remembers your passwords so you can use a different one everywhere — free, download it from bitwarden.com
items.summary: Reusing the same password everywhere is how one leaked password empties an email account, then a bank account. **Bitwarden** is a free password manager: it remembers every password so you only need one strong master password. Download it free at **bitwarden.com**, install it, and let it save passwords as you sign in. It takes about ten minutes to set up, works on your browser, and there's no paid plan needed for the basics.

items.title: Scans of 153 Million Driver's Licenses Are Being Sold Online
items.summary: Criminals are selling pictures of more than 153 million driver's licenses stolen from a company that checks IDs for car rentals and stores — the FBI is investigating. With your license picture, a stranger can open cards or loans in your name. Do this today: pull your free credit report at annualcreditreport.com and freeze your credit for free at Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion — it stops new accounts cold. Expect a second wave: scam emails and calls offering to "help" you with this breach. Hang up and delete.

items.title: That "unpaid SunPass toll" text is fake — delete it and check your real balance at sunpass.com
items.summary: The real SunPass never demands payment over a text message, and Florida's Attorney General has shut down fake toll sites before. Don't tap the link — delete the message, then check what you actually owe by signing in at **sunpass.com** or calling 1-888-TOLL-FLA (1-888-865-5352). Report the message free at **reportfraud.ftc.gov**.

items.title: Windows 10 computers no longer get free security updates — check Windows Update for your free Windows 11 offer
items.summary: On a Windows 10 PC, click **Start > Settings > Update & Security > Windows Update** and choose **Check for updates**. If your PC can run Windows 11, Microsoft's free offer appears right there — no purchase, no new computer, and your files stay put. If you see an offer for "Extended Security Updates" instead, that's Microsoft's safety net for older PCs — and it doesn't last forever.

items.title: Fake 'Are You Human?' Checks Are Running Hidden Commands on Computers
items.summary: Those little boxes websites use to check "Are you human?" — scammers are putting up fakes. They ask you to press the Windows key and R, paste a code, and press Enter "to verify." What really happens is a hidden command runs that can sneak a bad program in or open a doorway into your computer. Microsoft and the FTC are warning about this trick right now. A real human check never asks you to run anything. If you see that, close the tab.

items.title: 153 million driver's licenses were stolen — check your free credit report at annualcreditreport.com
items.summary: News broke this week that an identity-theft service is selling scanned driver's licenses for more than 153 million Americans and Canadians — and the FBI is investigating the company that collected them. Pull your free credit report at **annualcreditreport.com** (it's free every week, no catch), and freeze your credit for free at **Equifax**, **Experian**, and **TransUnion** so nobody can open a card or loan in your name.

items.title: Firefox's new update shows how many trackers it blocked right in the address bar — free at firefox.com
items.summary: **Firefox**'s latest version, out September 1, puts a counter right in the address bar that shows how many ad trackers it stopped, and it loads pages faster with new AI help features on top. If you already use Firefox, it updates itself automatically — or download it free at **firefox.com**. Takes 2 minutes.
